report.body:
A Civil Police investigation in Água Clara led to the seizure of about 54.64 kg
of drugs and the detention of five men. The operation began after Military
Police received an anonymous tip that a VW Gol was being used to sell drugs in
the urban area. Officers located the vehicle, and the driver tried to flee
when he saw the patrol car but was caught after a chase of a few blocks.

In the car, officers found a portion of a cocaine-like substance. At the
driver's home, officers found three more portions of marijuana totalling about
20 grams, plus a precision scale. At a second address found through the
investigation, officers seized 59 marijuana tablets weighing about 54 kg.
Two men aged 18 and 20 were arrested in flagrante at that address.

Officers later seized about 500 grams of marijuana and a precision scale from a
22-year-old suspect. In a bag, officers found 120 grams of cocaine divided
into 19 portions, which investigators said the first suspect had discarded
during the first stop. Four men were arrested in flagrante for drug
trafficking and association for trafficking, and a fifth was captured on an
arrest warrant. Officers also seized a car, a motorcycle, three precision
scales, three mobile phones, packaging material and about R$250 in cash.
The operation involved the integrated participation of the Civil and Military
police. Those involved were taken to the Água Clara Civil Police station
for legal procedures.

worker to six years of aggravated imprisonment for possessing hashish for
trafficking in the Badr police district. The referral order said she held
hashish for trafficking on 22 April 2026 in the Badr police district without

anti-drug schedules. The verdict was issued by a panel headed by Wagih
Hamza Shuqweir with judges Yasser Mohamed Youssef, Sameh Abdel Ghani Al-Antably

Sohag Criminal Court sentenced three men to death by hanging for possessing
hashish with intent to traffic in Al-Maragha district. The court also
convicted them of possessing a sharp scalpel-like tool without lawful
justification. The three defendants are from Ghonayem in Assiut
Governorate. The case was registered as Maragha felony 16693 of 2025 and
North Sohag general case 3346 of 2025.

Central Upper Egypt anti-narcotics officers arrested the men after prosecution
permission to arrest and search the first defendant. The chemical
laboratory confirmed the seized brown material was hashish in three lots of 80,
150 and 50 pieces, totalling 280 pieces, plus a plastic sack bearing drug
traces. Prosecutors charged all three with possessing hashish with intent
to traffic and using cars to transport and promote it. Prosecutors also
charged the first defendant with possessing a scalpel without lawful
justification after drugs were found in a seized car under his control.

After hearing arguments the court referred the defendants' papers to the Grand
Mufti for the religious opinion on execution by hanging. After the Mufti's
opinion arrived, the court issued its final verdict executing all three by
hanging by unanimous vote. The court ordered them to pay costs and
confiscated the seizures.

report.body:
Catalan police officers from the Mossos d'Esquadra criminal investigation
division arrested seven men aged 29 to 55 on 1 October 2026 over alleged links
to a drug-trafficking organisation. The operation took place in an
industrial warehouse in Cabanes, Girona, where officers seized 8,025 kg of
hashish. The arrests followed an investigation by the Sant Feliu de
Llobregat drug unit, which had identified the warehouse as used solely for
storing and distributing drugs. That inquiry had begun in June 2026 after
officers intercepted a van carrying about 2,400 kg of hashish in Viladecans.

In early October surveillance detected repeated movements of people and vans and
the arrival of an articulated lorry at the warehouse. Officers saw people
tampering with the vehicles' original number plates and fitting others with
cable ties, apparently to hinder identification. With support from the
Girona ARRO unit, officers entered the building and found seven people unloading
pallets from the trailer to move the hashish into vans for later distribution. The hashish was hidden among lawful cargo inside large raffia sacks filled
with shredded rubber, a system used to hinder detection at police or customs
checks.

Police valued the seized hashish at more than 16.2 million euros on the illicit
market. The 8 tonnes represented a significant share of the nearly 14,900
kg of this drug the Mossos had seized in 2026 up to 1 October. During the
search officers also found a firearm in one of the detainees' vans. The
seven detainees were placed before the Figueres court, the investigation remains
open and further arrests were not ruled out. Four of the seven were
remanded in provisional custody without bail and the other three were released
on bail.

report.body:
Spain's UDYCO drug unit arrested a truck driver at the port of Ceuta carrying a
stash of hashish hidden in a sophisticated false bottom. Officers
intercepted the truck on the port road at the Muelle de Poniente and searched it
with support from the UPR prevention unit and the canine group. They found
the hashish and detained the driver, showing him the drugs found in the vehicle
he was driving.

The truck appeared empty and was heading toward boarding for Spain when a
specialist drugs dog alerted, prompting an exhaustive hours-long search inside
and outside the vehicle. After the hours-long detailed inspection, officers
found a large number of bags full of hashish inside the truck's structure.
Officers recovered numerous bags of hashish from the trailer's false bottom,
with first estimates putting the haul above 300 kilograms although police gave
no official weight. The submitted account describes the seizure as about
300 kilograms of hashish arriving from Morocco.

The handcuffed driver was taken to police headquarters and placed under
investigation for an offence against public health. The judicial authority ordered his imprisonment after the Friday detention in Ceuta with the heavy vehicle loaded with hashish. The truck driver detained by the UDYCO in Ceuta was brought before the court on Sunday and remanded in preventive custody for an offence against public health. Police link the
operation to open UDYCO investigations into groups moving hashish from Ceuta to
mainland Spain in heavy vehicles with hidden compartments. The investigation remains open amid suspicion of larger drug loads and of heavy vehicles hidden in spaces used as hashish stores.

report.body:
Spain's National Police arrested four men and one woman in Palma as alleged
members of a group dedicated to drug trafficking. The operation closed a
months-long investigation by the National Police's Grupo I de Estupefacientes
and ended with five arrests, according to a police statement.

Officers intercepted a parcel addressed to a Palma resident that held 24 kilos
of hashish and arrested its recipient on suspicion of drug trafficking. In
the main suspect's home officers found 36 kilos of hashish, an air rifle with a
silencer and about 10,000 euros in cash, and arrested the man and a woman on
suspicion of drug trafficking and membership of a criminal group or
organisation. In a second home officers arrested a man suspected of storing
and transporting drugs and found two kilos of cocaine, further doses, cutting
substance, a pistol with nine-millimetre cartridges and a bow with arrows.
Officers also found a hydraulic press allegedly used to compress cocaine.

A fifth person was arrested in connection with the case, which police believe
involved distributing drugs to third parties for smaller-scale sale, and the
investigation remains open with further arrests not ruled out. Officers
from the Prevention and Reaction Unit, Grupo II de Estupefacientes and the dog
handlers assisted in the two house searches.

report.body:
Customs officers stopped a tourist vehicle returning from Spain on a roundabout
at Saint-Lary-Soulan on the evening of 28 September 2026 and arrested its
Ukrainian driver. The driver was a Ukrainian living in Poland with no
criminal record. He admitted accepting 3,000 euros to collect the cannabis
in Alicante and drive it to Poland. He was tried on 1 October 2026 by the
criminal court in Tarbes. The court sentenced him to 24 months in prison
and banned him from French territory for ten years.

Officers found 32 heat-sealed bags holding 32.8 kg of cannabis herb hidden in
two metal compartments under non-original carpet on the vehicle's floor.
Customs said an abnormal thickness in the vehicle's floor hid two compartments
fitted under the front seats. The court imposed a customs fine of 131,200
euros for carrying narcotics without proper documentation. It added a
second customs fine of 405 euros for customs money laundering, bringing the
fines to 131,605 euros. The court ordered confiscation of the 32.8 kg of
cannabis. It also confiscated 405 euros in cash, two telephones and a
computer.

The car had come from Spain through the Aragnouet-Bielsa tunnel. Officers
also found cloths soaked in white spirit used to mask the drug smell. The
court proposed a sentence adjustment through conditional release with
deportation.

attempts.decision_title: South Africa cannabis legalisation belongs to CFI history
attempts.explanation: The Al Jazeera article reports South Africa's Cannabis for Private Purposes Act, signed by President Cyril Ramaphosa, which removed cannabis from the list of outlawed narcotics and made adult grow and use lawful while sale remains illegal except on medical prescription. A change in the law, including legalisation of use, belongs to the CFI history under the tracker's scope rules, not to a tracker enforcement report. No single raid, seizure, arrest, trial or sentence is the subject of this article, so there is no tracker event to draft.
